articles.title: Philippines exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan to protect undersea cables
articles.summary: The Philippines is exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan on protecting undersea cables and addressing "gray-zone" activity, despite Manila's one-China policy, which recognizes Beijing and not…

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 2:18pm

WASHINGTON — The Philippines is exploring deeper cooperation with Taiwan on protecting undersea cables and addressing "gray-zone" activity, despite Manila's one-China policy, which recognizes Beijing and not Taipei, a Philippine diplomat said on Wednesday.

The Philippines and Taiwan have repeatedly complained about Chinese activities designed to pressure the countries without direct confrontation. China claims Taiwan as its own territory and has overlapping claims with both Taiwan and the Philippines in the South China Sea.

Felipe F. Carino III, Manila's deputy chief of mission in Washington, told a seminar this "pragmatic and practical approach" with Taiwan was necessary to protect mutual interests in the Bashi Channel between Taiwan and the Philippines.
Speaking to Washington's Center for a New American Security, Carino linked cable security to South China Sea tensions, but did not mention China by name.
He said security of undersea cables was vital given that they carried nearly all intercontinental data flows "and that 60-67% of cyber incidents happen in our region."

"These are very important features that should be protected, so much so that we are exploring deeper cooperation with our friends in Taiwan," Carino said, adding that the Philippines was doing so "notwithstanding our one China policy."

He said the Philippines and Taiwan were exploring "practical and more pragmatic approaches in cooperation, including knowledge-sharing and capacity building" and added: "We see this cooperation leading towards ... addressing the gray-zone issues in our part of the world."

Asked if this cooperation could include joint patrols or accountability for vessels that disrupt communications, Carino said he did not have details, but said: "I'm sure that this is a constantly evolving cooperation, and some of the things that you mentioned may be actually coming to fruition."

Taipei has stepped up efforts to protect undersea communications links, which are vital to the island's connections to the rest of the world, after several incidents involving cables and China-linked vessels.

This month, the Philippine Coast Guard said it had deployed its largest vessel and an aircraft to challenge a Chinese research ship operating off northern Batanes province near undersea cable corridors.

At the same seminar, Andrea Yang, Taiwan's deputy representative in Washington, referred to the jailing in Taiwan of a Chinese ship captain over damage to an undersea cable. She said Taiwan would put more resources into developing unmanned systems to improve maritime surveillance.
Yang said interference with undersea cables was an issue that should be taken up by the United Nations, which should consider mechanisms to prevent "bad behavior." — Reuters

articles.title: Divide and conquer? Teodoro says China meddling with Philippine politics
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro on Thursday said China is already meddling with Philippine politics as more Filipinos turn against each other.

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 2:18pm
Defense Secretary Gilberto “Gibo” Teodoro on Thursday said China is already meddling in Philippine politics as more Filipinos turn against each other.

“Pinaratangan na nila ako na personal political motive. Nakikialam na sila sa politika dito, hindi na diplomasya ang pinag-uusapan dito. They are already wading into the internal affairs ng Pilipinas at hindi…palalampasin ito,” Teodoro said in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.

(They have accused me of a personal political motive. They are meddling with the politics here, it is no longer about diplomacy. They are already wading into the internal affairs of the Philippines and this… should not be allowed to pass.)
Asked if there was an effort to divide and conquer, Teodoro said “definitely”.

“Made-de-escalate ito kung manindigan ang Pilipino laban sa kanila, kasi niloloko na tayo nitong mga ito, very obvious na 'to, at pinaghihiwa-hiwalay na tayo. Ang escalation ay hindi nanggagaling sa atin. Factual lang naman ang sinasabi natin laban sa kanila,” he added.

(This will be de-escalated if Filipinos stand up against them, because we are being fooled by them; it is very obvious that we are being divided. The escalation did not come from us. Everything we say against them is true.)

Jing has been drawing criticism after saying last week that China would win if it used force in the West Philippine Sea, something that he said his country would not do. However, some government officials have defended Jing, including Senator Robin Padilla, who claimed that the envoy was a gentleman.
“Opinyon ni Senator Robin iyon, pero opinyon ng nakararami, hindi eh,” Teodoro said.
(That is Senator Robin’s opinion, but the opinion of many is that he is not.)
Legislators from both chambers of Congress have filed their respective resolutions urging President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to declare Jing as persona non grata.
Following Jing’s comments, the Chinese Embassy has also targeted several Filipino personalities, even going as far as “banning” the House lawmakers behind the resolution from going to China.
Teodoro said that while Jing’s behavior is unacceptable, there were many things for Marcos to consider before he could decide to expel the envoy.
After all, Jing was only acting on the Chinese government’s orders, he added.

“Okay, palitan mo ‘man 'yan. Kung 'yung papalit, ganun pa rin ang ginagawa…Anong silbi? Kaya kailangan, 'yung solusyon dito, matigil 'yung gawain nila at maipaliwanag sa kanila na may hantungan ang pwede nilang gawin dito. Wala sa tao 'yun,” Teodoro said.

(Okay, replace him. But if the person they replace him with is also doing the same thing… then what is the use? So what is needed, the solution here is to stop what they are doing, and explain to them that they have limitations. This is not with the person.)
The Palace earlier stated that Marcos is not inclined to expel Jing, but maintained that this did not mean that the Philippines was relinquishing its claim on the West Philippine Sea.—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election
articles.summary: Disaffection has often driven down turnout among Arab Israelis, but there is a strong push to get rid of the right-wing governing coalition.

blocks.text: Students in Nazareth are handing out leaflets encouraging Arab Israelis to vote in next week's election
ByYolande Knell
Middle East correspondentReporting fromNazareth

At rush hour in Nazareth, the largest Arab-majority city in Israel, students are handing out leaflets by the roadside urging motorists to vote in next week's closely fought, general election. Polls indicate that Arab parties could be left holding a critical balance of power.

Disaffection has often driven down past turnout among Arab Israelis - who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. But this election, there is a strong push to get rid of the most right-wing governing coalition in the country's history - an alliance between veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties.

"I see it as our duty to bring down this extremist government. They treat us as second-class," says Arkan Badran, 23, who is with the students giving out flyers. "I call on all young men and women to vote for Arab lists, which represent us, because this is our future."

blocks.caption: Image caption, All but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out forming a coalition government with Arab parties

blocks.text: All but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out forming a coalition government with Arab parties
Most opinion polls indicate that neither Netanyahu and his partners nor the main "Change Bloc", led by centre-right former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a parliamentary majority.

If they are right, after the election anti-Netanyahu parties wanting to form a governing coalition would either have to go back on pledges not to work with the prime minister or make a deal with Arab-majority lists.
A major sticking point is that Eisenkot has so far ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values.

Israel's politics and society have been changed by the deadly, unprecedented Hamas-led assault on the country on 7 October 2023, and subsequent war in Gaza. There is increased mistrust of and hostility towards the country's Arab minority.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis

blocks.text: Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis

"After October 7, we were treated as enemies of this country," says Suha Salman Mousa of the Mossawa Centre in Nazareth, which advocates for equal rights for Arab citizens. "There was shrinking space for freedom of speech. There were major arrests, there was also firing of people from their workplaces because they put something on social media or they went out against the war on Gaza."

Salman Mousa accuses ministers of "systematic discrimination and incitement" against Arab Israelis. Civil society groups say they have disproportionately cut budgets for Arab communities. The government says reductions are needed to fund wartime defence and security spending.
There have also been politicised campaigns against Arab physicians working in Israeli hospitals and racially motivated attacks on Arab bus drivers by Jewish Israelis.

Some electioneering has sought to capitalise by deepening social divisions. The far-right Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, has vowed to "Judaise" parts of the northern Galilee and southern Negev regions where most Arabs live, likening this to expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank.

The majority of Arab Israelis are descendants of Palestinians who remained within what became Israel during the war that surrounded the creation of the state in 1948, when hundreds of thousands were forced from or fled their homes. Israel's current government often frames them as a threat to the state's Jewish identity. Recently, the prime minister has claimed that his rivals plan to team up with Arabs and form a "dangerous government".

To make this point, his campaign has put up billboards, including one at a road junction at the main entrance to Nazareth. They suggest a choice between: "Right or Palestine" - with pictures of main opposition figures, including right-wingers, depicted as representing the latter not the former. The Netanyahu campaign has also used AI-generated videos to present his opponents embracing Arab leaders.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Radio Nas anchor Mohammed Magadli says Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to delegitimise Arab parties

blocks.text: Radio Nas anchor Mohammed Magadli says Benjamin Netanyahu is trying to delegitimise Arab parties

At Radio Nas, a popular Arabic-language station in Nazareth, I meet news anchor Mohammed Magadli, who is also an analyst for Israel's Channel 12. His father, Raleb Magadli, served as Israel's first Muslim minister between 2007 and 2009, representing the Labour party.
I ask the younger Magadli what he makes of Change Bloc leaders refusing to join forces with Arab parties.

"In a word its racism. But if we're trying to explain why, it's because of the political interests of Benjamin Netanyahu," he says. "He's trying all the time to pull the legitimacy of the Arab parties - because they're Arab, because they're Palestinian. This is affecting the majority of the Jewish parties in Israel."

Polls this week have suggested that both Eisenkot's bloc and Netanyahu's religious-nationalist bloc could each win around 50 seats of the 120 in Israel's parliament while 13 or 14 seats in total could go to Arab-majority groupings.
These are the Joint Arab List, a coalition of Hadash, Balad and Taal, and the smaller United Arab List, an Islamist party headed by politician Mansour Abbas.

blocks.caption: Image caption, United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas wants Arab parties to reach a "position of influence"

blocks.text: United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas wants Arab parties to reach a "position of influence"

While Abbas's party was originally created as part of the Islamic Movement in Israel - which has socially conservative values - he has become known for joining with Jewish partners. He prioritises solving the problems of Arab Israelis and speaks relatively little of Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
Abbas has had a taste of power. In 2021, he became a minister in a previous, short-lived Israeli government led by Naftali Bennett - now a right-wing member of Eisenkot's bloc.

For this election, he has taken the surprise step of giving the number two position on his slate to a Jewish former police official and centrist member of parliament, Yoav Segalovitz. Abbas believes Eisenkot and others will be more open to an alliance with his party after the election and insists he wants to join the next government.

"We've reached the conclusion that parliamentary representation is not enough to serve Arab society. We decided to take responsibility, to become part of the solution to our problems and to offer hope to both Arabs and Jews," he tells me.
"That's why our approach has been driven by a desire to reach a position of influence, not merely representation."

blocks.caption: Image caption, The Joint List talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace Netanyahu's government

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
The Joint List talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace Netanyahu's government

Meanwhile, the Joint List - which is made up of secular parties and advocates for equal rights for Arab Israelis, an end to Israeli military occupation of Palestinian territories, and a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict - aims to wield a position of influence within the opposition.
It talks of providing an electoral "safety net" to those who could replace the Netanyahu government, in return for support on important policies.
A main issue in this election for Arab Israelis is rampant gang crime.
In September, a poll by the Israel Democracy Institute think tank found that this was the most important factor for 53.5% of Arab citizens when deciding which party to vote for.

Murders within the community reached a record high of 252 last year – about five times higher than the number of Jewish Israelis who were killed, according to the Abraham Initiatives, a Jewish-Arab organisation that promotes coexistence.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Arab Israelis accuse the government of inaction on the issue of gang crime

blocks.text: Arab Israelis accuse the government of inaction on the issue of gang crime
In Jaffa, a mixed Arab-Jewish neighbourhood which is now joined to Tel Aviv, Ziad Samouni shows me where his son, Hussein, was shot dead by two gunmen on a motorcycle near his home last November.
No arrests have been made in his case. With a low percentage of cases solved, Arab-Israelis accuse the government of inaction.

"It seems they're interested in making sure we reach a situation where the killer is never caught, allowing Arabs in Arab society to keep killing one another," says Samouni, who is now part of a support group, Israeli-Palestinian Bereaved Families for Peace.
The Israeli police told the BBC its investigation into Hussein's murder remained active, adding that it took "every case of violence and crime with the utmost seriousness."
"As a father who's lost a son, of course, I want this bloodshed to end," Samouni tells me. "I wish every Arab citizen who believes there needs to be a change sees that this is a time to go to vote."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Ziad Samouni's son Hussein (2nd L) was shot dead last November but no arrests have been made

blocks.text: Image source, Ziad Samouni
Ziad Samouni's son Hussein (2nd L) was shot dead last November but no arrests have been made
This month, Israel's Supreme Court overruled a decision by the Central Elections Committee to disqualify the United Arab List and the Joint List as well as two of their members.

The committee, which is dominated by the governing coalition, argued that they broke a law banning candidates who deny the existence of Israel as a Jewish state. The parties and their representatives strongly denied it.
With just days to go before voting, back in Nazareth, some motorists display flags for their preferred party on their cars.
The stakes are high in this election: Arab citizens could yet decide who wields power in Israel, and they also see this vote as key to their own future in the country.

articles.title: Boos, heckling greet Brady Tkachuk at 1st NHL game back in Ottawa
articles.summary: A chorus of boos awaited Former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk as he made his return to the ice at Canadian Tire Centre Wednesday night.

image.caption: Florida Panthers' Brady Tkachuk skates during warmups prior to an NHL hockey game against the Ottawa Senators in Ottawa, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. (Keito Newman/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Ottawa·New
A chorus of boos awaited Former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk as he made his return to the ice at Canadian Tire Centre Wednesday night.
Deal with the Florida Panthers in June sent Tkachuk to play in the Sunshine State
A chorus of boos awaited former Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk as he made his return to the ice at Canadian Tire Centre Wednesday night.
It was a packed stadium of vocal Sens fans who did not hold back in letting Tkachuk know how they feel about him.
"He's a traitor, there's not much else to say," said fan Jack Kelso.
"He promised he'd give us the [Stanley Cup], but he left."
Earlier this year, the 27-year-old requested a trade to join the Florida Panthers alongside his older brother and podcast co-host, a move that was unpopular with many fans.
Nearly every time Tkachuk took the ice, or touched the puck, chants, often profane in nature, erupted through the stadium.
"I was expecting it, I just didn't think it would be this much," said fan Lesley Miller.
Senators fans Elissa Robillard, left, and Lesley Miller, right, said there was a big reaction to Brady Tkachuk's return to Ottawa. (Emma Weller/CBC)
A number of attendees also altered their Tkachuk jerseys to showcase their new upset with the player, with some replacing his name with that of the team's new captain Thomas Chabot.
Others chose to throw their jerseys onto the ice.
On an episode of his Wingmen podcast, Tkachuk committed to donating any Sens jerseys tossed on the ice by upset fans to the Boys and Girls Club of Ottawa.
Ottawa Senators fans wore altered jerseys of former Senators player Brady Tkachuk at the game between the Senators and the Florida Panthers in Ottawa. (The Canadian Press/Lisa Wallace)
During the game, a video tribute was made to Tkachuk, who waved to the crowd amid the chants.
Shortly after, he scored the first goal of the night in a power-play goal midway through the first period.
The Sens bounced back, winning the game 5-1.
Tkachuk focuses on fun
After the game, Tkachuk said he has no hard feeling towards anyone and just tried to enjoy the experience.
"It's new, those were my teammates not too long ago," he said.
"It was nice to be in front of this passionate fan base," he added when asked about the fan's reaction to his return.
Travis Green, head coach of the Ottawa Senators, said the game felt "as close to a playoff game as you're gonna get."
"It was very emotional, physical, was a hard fought game and I thought our team was excellent tonight," he said.
Tkachuk spent eight seasons with the Senators after being drafted fourth overall in 2018.
He is set to return to the Canadian Tire Centre on March 18.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jenna Legge is a reporter with CBC in Ottawa. Before that, she worked as a journalist on Prince Edward Island, with earlier stints in Winnipeg and Toronto. She holds a master's degree in international journalism from City University of London, and also studied journalism, law and political science at Carleton University. She can be reached at jenna.legge@cbc.ca
With files from Emma Weller

articles.title: Ukraine, Russia trade strikes after Witkoff talks
articles.summary: Soon after Putin and Zelenskyy expressed willingness to resume US-mediated talks, Russia and Ukraine traded major attacks on each other's capitals.

image.caption: Kyiv's ability to defend against Russian drones and missiles has been reportedly limited after Elon Musk's Starlink restricted its speed for Ukraine's militaryImage: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia and Ukraine traded major attacks overnight, authorities from both countries said on Thursday, shortly after US envoy Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.
Missiles struck Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, wounding at least 15 people, eight of whom have been hospitalized, city authorities said.
The subway infrastructure on the Southern Bridge over the Dnipro river in Kyiv was also damaged, Mayor ⁠Vitali ​Klitschko ​said ​on Telegram.

blocks.caption: Ukraine's airforce warned of Russian missiles and instructed residents to take shelterImage: Evgeniy Maloletka/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Another Russian strike killed a woman and injured four others in the Kharkiv region in northeast Ukraine, regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram. A drone also hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure in the Poltava region, local authorities said without providing more details.
Meanwhile, Moscow's mayor said that 630 drones were launched towards the region overnight, wounding at least two people.
"Most of them were destroyed by air defense systems," Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on social media. Of these, 163 drones had been approaching the capital city, he added.
In western Russia's Lipetsk city, a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Igor Artamonov said on Telegram.
Strikes after US attempts mediation

The latest round of strikes came after US special envoy Witkoff held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway earlier this week, followed by talks with Putin in Russia on Wednesday.
The Trump administration has attempted to mediate between the two sides to end the conflict that began with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
US aims for new round of Russia-Ukraine negotiations

Putin agreed "in principle" to resume US-mediated peace talks with Kyiv as soon as next month. Zelenskyy, too, said on Wednesday that Ukraine supported a US proposal for trilateral talks at the negotiators level to be held as soon as possible.

It was "the closest we've been" to ending the war, US President Donald Trump claimed after Witkoff's meeting with Putin. However, that did not stop the neighboring nations from keeping up a barrage of attacks.

articles.title: Witness says he saw Zaldy Co give Martin Romualdez clothes, not maleta
articles.summary: Prosecution witness Police Major Ermelo Dichoso Jr., a former security detail of ex-Rep. Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, testified Thursday that Co gifted ex-Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez…

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 12:50pm

Prosecution witness Police Major Ermelo Dichoso Jr., a former security detail of ex-Rep. Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, testified Thursday that Co gifted ex-Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez with clothes.

Dichoso made the testimony during Day 6 of the hearing on Romualdez’s bail petition amid the P7.4 billion plunder case filed against him alongside Co, Romualdez's personal assistant Joselyn Tragua Sereño, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation over alleged pocketing of kickbacks from government projects.
During cross examination of Romualdez’s counsels, Dichoso confirmed seeing Co give clothes to Romualdez as gift as stated in his judicial affidavit.
“Hindi po maleta [ang nakita ninyong inabot] (You didn’t see any suitcase being handed over)?” asked the defense counsel.
To which, Dichoso replied: “Hindi po, damit po (No, it was clothes).”

At the same time, Dichoso testified that he was with Co when the former lawmaker met with Romualdez and other lawmakers four times, including in Aguado in Manila and at the Manila Polo Club Townhouse which Dichoso said are properties of Romualdez.
Asked by Sandiganbayan Associate Justice Fritz delos Santos if there were cash deliveries made to Romualdez during these meetings, Dichoso said “No.”

Ahead of Dichoso taking the witness stand, Romualdez’s lawyers opposed the inclusion of his testimony by citing that the contents of Dichoso’s affidavit were mere hearsay or information he heard from other people.
In response, the prosecution said they were presenting Dichoso as witness “to prove the world “basura (garbage),” referring to money, was used by Co’s team. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: DFA calls out Chinese Embassy for series of 'undiplomatic' posts
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs has rebuked the Chinese Embassy in Manila over a string of increasingly combative social media posts targeting Filipino officials since the Chinese ambassador…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:42pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr (2nd R) holding talks with Chinese ambassador to Manila Jing Quan (2nd L) in Manila, after the diplomat was summoned to Malacanang presidential palace over a clash between the Chinese Coast Guard and the Philippine Navy on disputed South China Sea waters on July 20, which left two Filipino troops injured.
PCO / Released

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs has rebuked the Chinese Embassy in Manila over a string of "escalatory and undiplomatic" social media posts targeting Filipino officials since the Chinese ambassador remarked last week that China could “easily win” if it used force.

In a statement on Thursday, October 22, the department called out the embassy for what it says are statements that "erode mutual trust and confidence" and severely undermine efforts to stabilize and improve bilateral relations.

It reminded all diplomats accredited to the Philippines to exercise restraint and responsibility in public, "especially on social media," and said it reserved the right to take further diplomatic action. It did not say what that action could be.

"The recent public statements of the Embassy do not reflect the longstanding spirit of constructive engagement between the two countries and the two foreign ministries. Such statements are not conducive to good relations nor to the effective discharge of diplomatic functions," the DFA said.
Even so, the Philippines "values its relations" with China, the statement read.

Calls from lawmakers to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata have not stopped the embassy from churning out sharply worded posts, many of them aimed at the legislators seeking his expulsion.

The embassy has dialed up the provocative tone of its public statements since Jing arrived in December 2025, often assailing Defense Secretary Gibo Teodoro, Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson Jay Tarriela and other elected officials who criticize China's actions in the West Philippine Sea.

Two resolutions in the Senate and one filed by 10 House members have asked President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to expel Jing or ask Beijing to recall him. In turn, the embassy, in several posts, has dared lawmakers to go ahead with his expulsion and warned more Filipino officials would be barred from China if Jing were expelled.
On Tuesday, the embassy reposted a joint statement by House members calling for his removal with the caption, “Put on record. You are now on the list.”

The word war between the embassy and Philippine officials ramped up after Jing said in a chance interview with reporters on October 15: “If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force. You know, we love peace, and in this region, we enjoy the peace.”

This remark prompted the DFA to summon Jing on Monday. Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said the words of the ambassador were “provocative and unacceptable” and detrimental to the already sensitive relationship between the two countries.
The DFA has said declaring a diplomat persona non grata was an option of last resort.
In its statement Thursday, the DFA also reaffirmed the Philippines’ adherence to its One China Policy, after a post by the embassy asked the department to clarify Manila’s position on Taiwan.

"In response to recent postings on social media, the DFA reaffirms the Philippines’ continued adherence to its One China Policy, anchored on the 1975 Philippines-China Joint Communique," the DFA said.

"It underscores our consistent position that the People’s Republic of China is the sole legal government of China, and that we fully understand and respect the position of the Chinese Government that there is but one China and that Taiwan is an integral part of Chinese territory," it added.

articles.title: Signal No. 2 remains in 2 areas as Super Typhoon Rosal weakens
articles.summary: The super typhoon was last spotted 400 kilometers east of Basco, Batanes, moving west-northwestward at 20 kph.

blocks.text: Weather
October 22, 2026 | 12:09pm

ANILA, Philippines — Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 remains in effect over Batanes and the northeastern portion of the Babuyan Islands as Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) further weakened while moving west-northwestward over the Philippine Sea east of Batanes, the state weather bureau PAGASA said Thursday.
In its 11 a.m. bulletin on Thursday, October 22, PAGASA said Rosal was packing maximum sustained winds of 185 kilometers per hour near the center and gusts of up to 230 kph.
The super typhoon was last spotted 400 kilometers east of Basco, Batanes, moving west-northwestward at 20 kph.
Strong to typhoon-force winds extend up to 780 kilometers from the center.
Warning signals
PAGASA raised the following tropical cyclone wind signals:
Signal No. 2
Luzon

items: Batanes
Northeastern portion of Babuyan Islands

blocks.text: Residents in these areas may experience gale-force winds ranging from 62 to 88 kph within the next 24 hours, posing minor to moderate threats to life and property.
Signal No. 1

items: Rest of the Babuyan Islands
Mainland Cagayan
Eastern portion of Isabela (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, Dinapigue)
Ilocos Norte
Apayao

blocks.text: Residents in these areas may experience strong winds ranging from 39 to 61 kph within the next 36 hours, posing minimal to minor threats to life and property.

PAGASA said Signal No. 3 is the highest wind signal that may be raised during Rosal's passage, particularly over Batanes. However, the possibility of raising Signal No. 3 will decrease if the typhoon takes a more north-northwestward track.
The northeast monsoon and Rosal's outer circulation will also bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas:

items: Thursday, October 22: Most of Luzon and the Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Northern Mindanao, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Sarangani, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental.
Friday, October 23: Most of Luzon and the Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Camiguin, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental.
Saturday, October 24: Batanes, Babuyan Islands, Ilocos Norte, Polillo Islands, Bicol Region, Romblon, Capiz, Iloilo and Negros Occidental.

blocks.text: PAGASA advised the public to refer to Weather Advisory No. 8, issued at 11 a.m. Thursday, for the heavy rainfall outlook due to Rosal.
Sea conditions
A gale warning is in effect over the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon.
Very rough to very high seas, with waves reaching up to 12 meters, are expected along the northern and eastern seaboards of Batanes.
Waves may reach up to 9 meters along the seaboard of the Babuyan Islands, the remaining seaboard of Batanes and the northeastern seaboard of mainland Cagayan.

Seas may reach up to 7 meters along the remaining seaboard of mainland Cagayan and the seaboard of northern Isabela. Waves may reach up to 6 meters along the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte and the remaining seaboard of Isabela.

Waves may reach up to 5.5 meters along the remaining seaboard of Ilocos Norte, while seas may reach up to 4.5 meters along the seaboards of Ilocos Sur and northern Aurora, as well as the northern and eastern seaboards of the Polillo Islands.

PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types of vessels in areas where very rough to very high seas are expected. Mariners were advised to remain in port or seek shelter in a safe harbor until winds and waves subside.
Operators of small vessels, including motorbancas, were also advised against venturing out to sea in areas with rough seas, especially if their vessels are ill-equipped or they lack experience.
Track, intensity
Rosal is expected to continue moving generally northwestward until Thursday night before turning north-northwestward on Friday morning, October 23.
The tropical cyclone is forecast to recurve north-northeastward by Saturday, October 24.

On its forecast track, Rosal will be closest to Extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday afternoon and Friday morning before exiting the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or early Saturday.
PAGASA said Rosal will continue to gradually weaken and may be downgraded from a super typhoon to a typhoon within Thursday. By Saturday, it may further weaken into a severe tropical storm.
The weather bureau warned that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still affect areas outside the forecast track and that Rosal's path may still change.

articles.title: No purchase, no seats: Starbucks China rolls out new policy
articles.summary: Starbucks says it is improving customers' in-store experience as it competes with homegrown rivals.

blocks.text: Taking a seat at a Starbucks in China? Just make sure you're also ordering something there.
A new policy by Starbucks China takes effect across all its 8,000 stores on Thursday, making it mandatory for people to purchase items if they want to sit in its cafes.
Starbucks China said the move was part of efforts to improve the "in-store experience" for customers. The company is facing stiff competition from homegrown brands such as Luckin Coffee.
Reports of the new policy circulated this week, along with social media videos of what appear to be "purchase to sit" signs in Starbucks stores.
Many on Chinese social media welcomed the new policy.

"Finally, there won't be peak periods where people are just sitting there not ordering anything, drinking Luckin coffee, playing games and yelling on the phone," reads one of the top-liked comment on Weibo. "Every time I walk around, there's nowhere to sit,"
"There's nothing wrong with it. I'd feel awkward sitting there if I didn't make a purchase. I'd rather leave the seats for those who made purchases and need the seats," another Weibo user commented.
Starbucks stores around the world have been wrestling with non-paying seat-hoggers and other undesirable behaviour from customers.

Last month, a Starbucks store in Sichuan province sparked debate after video of its chained-up outdoor seats and tables were circulated on social media. It appeared to be an attempt to block people from sitting there without paying.
In South Korea, Starbucks has told customers to stop bringing "bulky items" into their stores, after some patrons reportedly hogged seats with printers and desktop computers in tow.

In North America, Starbucks reversed its open-door policy which for years allowed people to use their seats and toilets without buying anything, saying that it wanted to "prioritise" paying customers.

Since opening its first store there in 1999, China has become Starbucks' second-largest market. But it has faced stiff competition in recent years from Luckin and other local brands that offer cheaper products.

Luckin also offers a robust app-based ordering system that prioritises grab-and-go transactions, challenging Starbucks' model of a full cafe experience where people can sit down and enjoy their food and drinks.
In 2023, Luckin overtook Starbucks as China's largest coffee chain.
Starbucks said last year it would sell 60% stake of its business in China as part of a $4bn (£3.04bn) deal with investment firm Boyu Capital.

In another statement on Wednesday, Starbucks China said it was planning to increase staffing and improve digital systems at its stores, among other investments to "ensure customers receive timely and warm service even during peak hours".

articles.title: SolGen to seek partial reconsideration of SC ruling on past budgets
articles.summary: The Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) said Thursday it would seek clarification and partial reconsideration of certain parts of the Supreme Court (SC) decision which declared as unconstitutional…

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 12:01pm

The Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) said Thursday it would seek clarification and partial reconsideration of certain parts of the Supreme Court (SC) decision which declared as unconstitutional the national budget laws in 2024 and 2025, and legislated provisions relating to unprogrammed funds.
This came a day after Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said Malacañang "respectfully disagrees" with certain parts of the ruling, asking the high court to carefully review it.
The Palace said the OSG has been tasked to file the motion for reconsideration.

The OSG confirmed that it received a copy of the SC decision, which it said it respects. However, the OSG said it would challenge certain parts, "particularly the guardrails prescribed for the exercise of budgetary powers."

"The OSG agrees that safeguards are essential to ensure transparency, accountability, and fiscal discipline in the use of public funds. The complex challenge, however, lies in distinguishing the safeguards that are required by the Constitution from those whose formulation falls within the constitutionally provided powers of Congress and the Executive," it said.
EXPLAINER: SC voids multi-trillion-peso budget laws in 2024 and 2025. Now what?

"The OSG will respectfully seek clarification and partial reconsideration to ensure that the guardrails prescribed in the Decision remain consistent with this constitutional allocation of powers," it added.

In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court struck down the General Appropriations Acts (GAAs) for 2024 and 2025 after Congress added appropriations beyond what the President had recommended in the National Expenditure Program.

Specifically, the 2024 budget was voided due to a P449.5-billion increase in unprogrammed appropriations, while the 2025 budget was struck down because of the additional P17.99 billion for the Special Road Fund of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

The High Court likewise deemed as unconstitutional Special Provisions 1(a) and (b), Chapter XLIII in the 2026 GAA authorizing unprogrammed appropriations. It then set conditions that would allow the such appropriations to be constitutional.

The OSG noted that the 12 separate opinions accompanying the SC decision "reflect the complexity of the constitutional questions presented and the differing judicial perspectives on their resolution."
The OSG said it would carefully consider such opinions in its further action. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: North Korea prepares to restart propaganda loudspeakers as ties sour with South
articles.summary:
Kim Yo-jong, sister of Kim Jong-un, issues warning after inspecting border fortifications against backdrop of rising tensions

Propaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to…

blocks.text: Propaganda loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be ready to restart within days along the entire border, Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, has said amid a worsening of ties between the two countries.
The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA on Thursday, came a day after she said the loudspeakers would be in operation along the whole border from some time in October.

Both North and South Korea have historically used giant loudspeakers to broadcast propaganda across the border, with the North in recent years playing haunting bestial howls, and the South opting for K-pop music ​and news criticising Pyongyang.

If the broadcasts resume, they would be the first loudspeaker exchange across the border in 16 months. South Korean president Lee Jae Myung suspended broadcasts from the southern side just days into his presidency in June 2025 to ease tensions with Pyongyang, and the military dismantled the speakers that August.

At a briefing on Thursday, a defence ministry spokesperson in Seoul said that if North Korea went ahead, “naturally there would have to be a proportional measure”, but made clear no decision had been made.

blocks.caption: A North Korean military guard post featuring loudspeakers, seen in February 2026.  Photograph: Ahn Young-joon/AP

blocks.text: The joint chiefs of staff said routine maintenance of the North’s loudspeakers had been observed before Kim Yo-jong’s statements.
Tensions between the two Koreas have risen since September, when a landmine blast south of the military demarcation line injured three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously.

Seoul and the UN command – which oversees the 1953 armistice that halted but did not end the Korean war – concluded it was a North Korean anti-personnel mine and an armistice violation. Pyongyang denied responsibility and called the incident a “self-staged farce”.

The loudspeaker threat comes as North Korea continues to fortify its side of the border. Since Kim Jong-un declared that the two Koreas were “two states hostile to each other” in December 2023, North Korea has laid mines, strung barbed wire and erected anti-tank barriers along the border.
On Wednesday, Kim Yo-jong inspected several fortification points along the border with Pak Jong-chon, a marshal and adviser to Pyongyang’s defence ministry.
The border had been “clearly blocked and turned into a fortress more thoroughly”, she said, adding that Kim Jong-un had told her it “should be a permanent line never to be crossed”.

Seoul says North Korean troops have repeatedly crossed the military demarcation line, the 250km line dividing the two Koreas, during the construction work, prompting South Korean soldiers to issue warnings over loudspeakers and fire warning shots.
North Korea has called the warning shots and broadcasts provocations by “armed rogues”.

articles.title: What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble?
articles.summary: AI uncovered long-hidden programming flaws, triggering a rare global cyber-security response.

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
ByOsmond Chia
Business reporter
For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in technology underpinning much of the internet.
It took artificial intelligence (AI) to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert.
The vulnerabilities lie within a programming language called PHP, which has been used internationally since the 2000s to build websites.

Governments and cyber-security agencies around the world scrambled to contain the fallout of this discovery on Wednesday, and have urged website operators to install a new emergency fix or consider taking their platforms offline.
Cyber-security firm Wiz - one of the companies whose researchers uncovered the vulnerabilities - described the flaws as the "most severe" ever detected by AI.
OpenAI, whose technology was used to find the flaws, called the discovery "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
What is the flaw?
Most people may not have heard of PHP - short for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor - but they most certainly interact with it daily.
PHP powers a vast number of platforms, including online shops, Wikipedia and WordPress – the content management system behind many websites like blogs.

When you visit a website like Wikipedia, PHP is the code that collects information you need and presents it in a way you can read on the web, Paul Spain, chief executive of Gorilla Cyber Security, told the BBC.
But due to a flaw that could allow attackers to take control of affected web servers without authentication and steal sensitive data, everything built on PHP was left exposed.
AI could make such attacks easier and faster, Spain said, estimating that the flaw could affect "millions and millions" of websites.
It would be "disastrous" if hackers or countries weaponised the flaw and seized private data from websites, said cyber-security researcher Jill Slay from the University of Adelaide.
What websites have been affected?
The alert has disrupted services globally, from gaming platforms to government portals and online forums.
That includes Wikimedia - the organisation behind the online encyclopaedia Wikipedia - which took down a number of its systems as a precautionary measure.
Sites and pages have been taken offline by the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC, with the Netherlands' cyber-security agency also pulling its website.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Websites like the University of Geneva's were taken offline on Wednesday

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
Websites like the University of Geneva's were taken offline on Wednesday
A number of Scotland's public organisations, including councils and health boards, have also taken their websites offline.
Some experts warn the vulnerability could leave poorly maintained websites, particularly those belonging to smaller organisations with limited security resources, at greater risk.
More attempts to exploit these flaws are likely in the coming weeks since the technical details are now being made public, cyber-security researcher Salil Kanhere from UNSW Sydney said.
What happened after the flaws were exposed?
Developers of the PHP platform on Wednesday rolled out patches to fix the vulnerabilities that had been lurking in their software for years.
"All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately," the company said.
Authorities and security organisations around the world have echoed those warnings to website operators to secure their platforms.

The US National Security Agency told all organisations that use PHP to take their systems offline if they were unable to patch them immediately, adding that the flaw could provide a "direct path" to exploit a system's database.
"These risks are serious enough to require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies," the agency said.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre gave similar advice and told organisations to check for "backdoors installed by an attacker".
Its counterparts in the EU and Australia have also issued similar alerts.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP

blocks.text: Image source, Bloomberg via Getty Images
Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP
"We have an urgent request for everyone to take action tonight," Takaichi wrote on X.
"If it is difficult to apply the fix patch promptly, temporarily suspending websites and similar measures can be considered an effective way to reduce risk," she said.
How is AI finding weak spots?
The vulnerabilities were found by researchers at the security firms Calif and Wiz.
The researchers used advanced AI tools that are able to analyse code and find flaws much faster than humans or older systems can.
"Modern software is incredibly complex, and some vulnerabilities can remain undetected for years," Kanhere said.
"The underlying bugs weren't new; what changed was our ability to find them," Kanhere said.
Details of the discovery leaked online this week, forcing the PHP platform's developers to rush out its announcement of the security flaw and its huge scale.
The incident "highlights how AI can uncover security flaws" but also how it can "help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits," OpenAI said in a blog post.
The ChatGPT-maker said it had released a program to check if the PHP platform is secure.

"Many of these flaws stem from the way software were built in the past, which were built for functionality and not with security in mind," said Ryan Ko, at the University of Queensland's Cyber Research Centre.
What can people do to safeguard themselves?
Website owners are being urged to secure their websites with the latest version of PHP.
The US National Security Agency has urged "heightened awareness" in the coming weeks and to closely monitor updates from software vendors.
"Vigilance in applying patches related to those systems is paramount," it said.
The onus lies mainly on website operators, but users should stay alert for any security advice issued by affected services, such as requests to change passwords, Kanhere said.
He warned people to be alert to any phishing messages exploiting the publicity around the incident too.

articles.title: SolGen seeks review of SC ruling on unprogrammed appropriations
articles.summary: The Office of the Solicitor General said it will seek clarification and partial reconsideration from the Supreme Court regarding its ruling on the constitutionality of unprogrammed appropriations.

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 11:47am
The main building of the Philippine Supreme Court in Manila as taken on December 13, 2024.
Philstar.com / Martin Ramos

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) said it will seek clarification and partial reconsideration from the Supreme Court regarding its ruling on the constitutionality of unprogrammed appropriations.
In a statement on Thursday, October 22, the OSG said that while it respects the High Court's ruling, it raised concerns over specific conditions imposed by the Court.
"The OSG agrees that safeguards are essential to ensure transparency, accountability, and fiscal discipline in the use of public funds," the OSG said.

"The complex challenge, however, lies in distinguishing the safeguards that are required by the Constitution from those whose formulation falls within the constitutionally provided powers of Congress and the Executive," it added.

The OSG said it will request the High Court to clarify and reconsider aspects of the ruling to ensure the prescribed safeguards do not inadvertently trample upon the budgetary discretion entrusted to the legislative and executive branches.
According to the OSG, the complexity of the case was underscored by the presence of twelve separate opinions issued alongside the main decision.
"The OSG will carefully consider these opinions in its further action," the OSG said.

The Supreme Court, in its ruling on October 7, declared unconstitutional provisions of the 2024, 2025, and 2026 General Appropriations Acts concerning unauthorized congressional increases in unprogrammed funds and specific special accounts.
The High Court emphasized that unprogrammed appropriations are not unconstitutional per se, as long as they comply with specific conditions.

While the Supreme Court affirmed the President's discretion to certify House Bill No. 8980 as urgent and upheld Congress's freedom to act on such certifications, it found that lawmakers violated Article VI, Section 25(1) of the Constitution by increasing the total proposed budget across both programmed and unprogrammed allocations.

Despite this constitutional violation, the Court applied the doctrine of operative fact, ensuring that irreversible programs under the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts carried out in good faith remain valid and intact for their beneficiaries.
Supreme Court justices filed separate opinions concurring with the final judgment while offering distinct legal views.

While they concurred that unprogrammed appropriations serve as a valid budgetary tool, their views diverged regarding the specific constitutional flaws identified, the scope of authority granted to the bicameral conference committee, and the practical consequences of striking down specific budget provisions.

articles.title: US embassy accuses Canada of election meddling ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed the claim, noting that it was the that US initiated trade actions against Canada.

blocks.text: The US Embassy in Ottawa has accused Canadian officials of election meddling ahead of the November midterms.

The embassy said Canadian leaders have brushed off concerns over "potential interference", and that ministers and premiers "openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances".
Canadian leaders, including Prime Minister Mark Carney, have dismissed the claims. Relations between the North American neighbours have hardened during second Trump administration.
The midterms will determine which political party controls both branches of the US Congress, which could have a significant impact on the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

The fact sheet released by the US Embassy on Wednesday alleges the Canadian government "brushes off concerns about potential interference in U.S. elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances".
It cites comments and actions, like meetings with US Democrats and calling for retaliatory tariffs against the US.

For example, it says that when Industry Minister Mélanie Joly was asked what she expected regarding tariffs if Democrats were to win midterm elections, she responded, "That's exactly why I'm meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates."

Ontario Premier Doug Ford pushed Canada's federal government, it states, to consider additional retaliatory tariffs on imports from "politically significant states to the current administration's base of support".
Asked on Wednesday about the allegations, Carney noted that it was the US that first initiated trade actions against Canada.
"We've responded to those to protect Canadian jobs, to protect Canadian companies and develop our economy," Carney said.
He said his government's response has been "in the interests of Canadian workers, Canadian families and the future of this economy".
Carney, who was announcing a nearly C$9bn ($6.2bn) aid package in response to US tariffs, was accompanied by both Joly and Ford.
Ford said that he has "no interest at all" in interfering in US elections.
"I'll tell you what the American people want. They want certainty, they want stability," Ford said, adding that he will focus on Ontario and Canada.
"The people of the United States will make that determination in the midterms," he said.
Last week, Minister Joly denied Canadian interference and said that Canadians "never accept that also being done to us in Canada", according to CBC.
She said that her recent visits to the US were "to attract investments" from American companies, which she plans to continue.

articles.title: Interviews for next chief justice begin
articles.summary: The JBC has begun public interviews for the country's next chief justice.

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 11:05am

Members of the Judicial and Bar Council panel Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, Sen. Kiko Pangilinan, Rep. Gerville Luistro, with other lawyers and retired justices conduct interviews for the position of chief justice on Oct. 22, 2026.
SC Office of the Spokesperson
MANILA, Philippines — Interviews for aspirants seeking to become the country's next chief justice began on Thursday, October 22.
The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) began its public interviews with two of the Supreme Court's most senior justices.
In the morning, the JBC started its interview of Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen. Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa is set to face the panel in the afternoon.
Both Leonen and Caguioa were appointed by former President Benigno Aquino III. They are the two most senior incumbent justices of the high court.

Among the JBC members present on the first day of interviews were Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, Sen. Kiko Pangilinan, Rep. Gerville Luistro of Batangas' 2nd District, retired Supreme Court Associate Justice Jose Catral Mendoza, retired Court of Tax Appeals Associate Justice Erlinda Piñera Uy, lawyer Jose Mejia and law professor Nesauro Firme.
The next round of interviews is scheduled for October 26, when Associate Justices Rodil Zalameda, Japar Dimaampao and Jose Midas Marquez are set to face the panel.
Former presidential candidate, lawyer and doctor Jose Montemayor also applied for the chief justice position.
However, Supreme Court spokesperson Camille Ting earlier said the JBC did not consider Montemayor for the position.
Gesmundo is set to retire on November 6 upon reaching the mandatory retirement age of 70.

His retirement will give President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. his first opportunity to appoint a chief justice. Marcos has so far appointed one justice to the Supreme Court, Associate Justice Raul Villanueva, in June 2025.

articles.title: Austrian, Swiss women kidnapped in Niger are freed — report
articles.summary: An Austrian woman and a Swiss woman kidnapped in Niger have been freed after 18 months in captivity, local reports say.

image.caption: The operation was reportedly overseen by Khalifa Haftar (seen in the photo here from 2024), the deputy commander-in-chief of Libya's armed forces.Image: Abdullah Doma/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Niger released two women, one Swiss and the other Austrian, after over a year of holding them captive, according to multiple reports.
The two women were flown out to Libya's eastern city of Benghazi, Libyan media outlets reported on Thursday.
The Austrian national, identified by Austrian authorities as Eva G., and the Swiss national, whom the Swiss foreign ministry has not previously named, were both abducted in Niger in 2025.
Eva G. is in her 70s, and the Swedish woman, identified by media outlets as Claudia Abbt, is 69 years old, according to reports.
Eva G. was kidnapped in the desert ⁠town of Agadez in central Niger, in January 2025. Abbt was abducted in April of 2025.
It was not immediately clear which group was holding them and what demands it had made.
Libyan news channel releases video of the two women freed from captivity
In a video released by Libya's al-Masar TV, the women appeared physically weakened.
Both women thanked the deputy commander-in-chief of Libya's armed forces, Khalifa Haftar, and his son, Saddam, for their release. Haftar reportedly oversaw the operation that freed the women.
"I had been held hostage for a year and nine months," Eva G. said, while Abbt said she was "happy to be free," also thanking Haftar.

Libya and Niger share a border hundreds of miles long, cutting through the Sahara Desert and connecting with Algeria and Chad on either side. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime ruler Moammar Gaddafi.
At the moment, two governments are vying for power there: a UN-recognized administration led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and its rival in the east, backed by Haftar.
Editor's note: DW has not yet independently verified the video released by the Libyan news channel that shows the two women, now freed, speaking to camera.

articles.title: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi threat
articles.summary: The US State Department has asked some US diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia because of the threat of Houthi attacks on the Gulf kingdom.

image.caption: Houthis have attacked several major Saudi airports, including the capital Riyadh's King Khalid Airport [FILE: Oct 8, 2026]Image: Social Media/REUTERS

blocks.text: At least one person was killed in a strike on a Saudi airport in the eastern city of Dammam on Wednesday, as Washington ordered some diplomats and family members to leave the Gulf country.
Saudi Arabia's revived war with the Iranian-backed Houthi rebels has intensified in recent weeks, with the Yemeni rebels targeting several major Saudi airports.
Saudi Arabia on the backfoot in the war against the Houthis
What do we know about the strike on the airport in Dammam?
The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said a strike on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday evening killed one person and injured eight others.
The authority added on X that the extent of the material damage to the airport was being assessed.
It did not say who was behind the attack and the Houthis did not claim responsibility.
Flight-tracking website Flightradar24 said flights from the airport were being diverted as operations came to a halt.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi Energy Ministry said forces successfully intercepted a drone targeting an oil facility, but that falling debris killed two people and injured two others. Those killed were identified by the ministry as a Filipino and a Nepali national.
US State Department orders partial evacuation of Saudi mission
Meanwhile, US State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said his department had issued an order for the departure of non-essential staff and family members at the US embassy in Riyadh.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott wrote on X.
Both Reuters and AFP news agencies cited unnamed sources as saying a similar order was also issued for other countries in the Gulf, with AFP listing the UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain.
Pigott denied the reports, saying they were "inaccurate" and that only employees in Saudi Arabia were ordered to leave.
The US has issued similar evacuation orders on more than one occasion this year amid the Iran war and Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the US-Israeli war against Tehran.
Houthi attacks on Saudi airports raise stakes for Washington
A four-year truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi rebels collapsed amid the Iran war, with Saudi Arabia experiencing near daily attacks this month.

articles.title: Some US diplomats told to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
articles.summary:
Reports emerge of similar withdrawals in UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid concerns about a return to conflict with Iran after US midterm elections

The US state department has ordered some…

blocks.text: The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, as the gulf kingdom faces a barrage of near-daily attacks, with at least three people killed at an airport and oilfield on Wednesday evening.

Attacks on “civilian airports and other critical infrastructure” by the Iranian-supported Houthis in Yemen were highlighted as the reason for the drawdown. State department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said: “The safety and security of department personnel and their families remain our highest priority.”

The state department said the order covered its embassy in Riyadh and its satellite consulates. The embassy had been badly damaged at the start of the US war on Iran and had been operating with only a skeleton staff for months, although in recent weeks some diplomats had returned.

The announcement comes as some media – including NBC and AFP – reported that families of US embassy personnel were also being withdrawn from the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, while the New York Times said the Trump administration was developing plans to restart the war on Iran.

However in his statement on Wednesday, Pigott described the reports of further withdrawals as “inaccurate” and stressed that the state department order was for the departure of staff and their families from Saudi Arabia only.

Saudi Arabia has faced a succession of deadly attacks from the Houthis over recent weeks, including a strike on Riyadh’s international airport that was the kingdom’s deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.
On Wednesday evening the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority announced that one Saudi resident was killed in attacks on King Fahad international airport in Dammam, on the Gulf near Bahrain and Qatar.

Eight people were injured and the airport also suffered some material damage, according to officials. Global flight-tracking service Flightradar24 said flights had been diverted away from the airport.

Separately, falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility in the country’s south-east also killed two people and injured a further two, the Saudi energy ministry said.

Neither attack was immediately claimed by the Houthis, but airports and oil facilities have been a major target of the militant group in their recent wave of missile and projectile strikes on Saudi Arabia.

The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran in late February. NBC reported that the US military has been quietly scaling back its presence at bases across the Middle East in recent days, however a spokesperson from US central command told the US outlet that service members are regularly moved to “optimize mission readiness”.
The withdrawal of staff from the region comes amid reports that Trump has been presented with plans for restarting strikes on Iran, after the midterm elections.

The New York Times reported that the US and Israel developed plans for a “short but intensive operation”, after defense secretary Peter Hegseth travelled to Israel earlier this week for meetings with prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Last week ⁠Trump said the US was looking to knock out Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain, a site linked to the country’s ⁠nuclear program, however the president has publicly said that he does not intend to restart the war before the 3 November elections.
With Reuters and Agence France-Presse

articles.title: Lawmakers hail Supreme Court ruling voiding billions in budget items
articles.summary: Lawmakers have welcomed the Supreme Court's ruling declaring key provisions of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Acts (GAA) unconstitutional, describing the decision as a decisive…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 8:09am
The logo of the Supreme Court at the Supreme Court Building in Manila.
Philstar.com / Ian Laqui

MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers have welcomed the Supreme Court's ruling declaring key provisions of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 General Appropriations Acts (GAA) unconstitutional, describing the decision as a decisive victory for public accountability.

The high court’s 121-page decision, released to the press on October 20, invalidated congressional increases totaling P449.5 billion in 2024 unprogrammed appropriations, a P17.99-billion addition to the 2025 Special Road Fund, and key provisions governing 2026 standby funds.
The court ruled that Congress committed a grave abuse of discretion by exceeding the constitutional cap on the executive’s total recommended appropriations.
Sen. Panfilo Lacson lauded the ruling's timing as the Senate prepares to review the House version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill.

"One good thing about the Supreme Court ruling is its timing. It couldn’t have come at a better time when the House version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill is undergoing scrutiny by the Senate," Lacson said.

Lacson, who was not a member of the Senate when the 2024 and 2025 national budgets were passed, warned of imminent friction between the two legislative chambers as the Senate addresses "red flags" in the proposed 2027 spending plan.

He indicated that the Senate may restore hundreds of billions of pesos in cuts and realignments introduced by the House, particularly regarding Foreign-Assisted Projects (FAPs) and flood control allocations.

Describing the ruling's historical impact, Lacson asserted that the 2024 and 2025 national budgets would "go down in history as the worst budgets ever passed by Congress," comparing their invalidation to the Supreme Court's landmark decision striking down the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP) under the 2013 GAA.
On the immediate practical consequences of the decision, Lacson clarified that funds remaining unspent may no longer be disbursed, while those already expended cannot be invalidated retroactively.
Sen. Leila de Lima, who served as a co-petitioner in the consolidated legal challenges against the 2026 unprogrammed appropriations, hailed the ruling as a major triumph in curbing fiscal abuse.
"This decision of the Supreme Court is a warning to those who conspire and plan to abuse Unprogrammed Appropriations for personal and political interests," De Lima said in Filipino.

"Starting with the 2022 GAA, the unprogrammed funds were growing out of control. It became a holding area for pork, where lawmakers could park projects, create artificial fiscal space, and redirect hundreds of billions to their pet allocations. The Supreme Court has closed that backdoor,” she added.

articles.title: The real reasons US politicians are getting older
articles.summary: No country for young men and women: why do older politicians seem to have such a tight grip on the US political system?

blocks.text: Twenty-seven-year-old Republican Riley Owen is one of the few candidates from Gen Z - aged in their early teens to late 20s - from either party running for Congress on 3 November.

Owen is running in a newly created district in Utah that experts say may lean towards the Democrats. He has championed issues including paid maternity leave, restrictions on congressional stock trading and environmental action - all issues that may appeal to Democratic supporters.

When he was confirmed as his party's candidate in the state's 1st congressional district, he walked on stage to Billy Joel's We Didn't Start the Fire, and argued that his generation needed to help renew the American Dream.

The gerontocracy is "a bipartisan issue", he says. "We've got people who have become career politicians, and they spend their lives in Congress." He says this is indicative of a system that is not delivering for Americans.
Owen says the big challenge he faces is the fact that money really talks in US politics. Research suggests campaign donors tend to prefer incumbent candidates.

Indeed, the campaign of his rival Ben McAdams - a 51-year-old Democrat who has previously served in Congress - has so far raised much more cash than Owen's. By mid-October, McAdams had raised over $2.6m (£1.9m), compared with $150,000 raised by Owen, according to records on the Federal Election Commission website.

Owen argues that his generation is uniquely well-placed to understand contemporary political issues, such as the challenges posed by tech. He also disputes any suggestion that a younger candidate necessarily lacks relevant experience - pointing to his own background as a military officer and a White House policy analyst. "I think in politics, just like in industry, we need what's called disruptive innovation," he says.

The age of America's top politicians has long been a talking point. In 1984 Reagan - who was then America's oldest president at age 73 - deflected scrutiny with a quip about the "youth and inexperience" of his opponent Walter Mondale, who was a sprightly 56.

In the US, individual states also have their own legislatures, with a Senate and a House, where many politicians make their start. Many current members of Congress spent years in state politics before running for a seat in Washington

For those young people who do end up in high-profile political positions, the next question is whether they can make a success of it, especially when it comes to parenthood. Over the summer, the stories of two high-profile young women working in Washington raised fresh questions around compatibility of the job with motherhood.
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, 37, a Democratic congresswoman who took office aged 29, announced that she had started the process of freezing her eggs.

Later the same week in August, Karoline Leavitt, 29, who was appointed the youngest ever White House press secretary almost two years earlier, said she would leave the Trump administration to spend more time with her family, including her newborn baby. She explained: "I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy and attention required of [being] the White House press secretary."

Only a handful of women have given birth while elected to Congress, while a few dozen lawmakers are mothers to children under the age of 18. The federal government, like many US employers, does not offer paid parental leave.

JD Vance, 42, one of the youngest vice-presidents in US history, recently acknowledged that having young children might impact on his own decision to run for the White House in 2028, saying: "We've got four little kids."

articles.title: Pope Leo will not need further cancer treatment — Vatican
articles.summary: Pope Leo's lung cancer surgery last week was a success, the Vatican said. The pope broke with traditions of secrecy around papal health issues after announcing he needed surgery to remove a nodule on…

image.caption: The 71-year-old pontiff thanked worshippers for their prayers during the weekly general audience at St. Peter's Square at the VaticanImage: Tiziana Fabi/AFP

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV will not require further cancer treatment, his doctors announced on Wednesday, after the pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer last week.
The Vatican cited the pope's doctors, Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora, as saying the pope's disease was localized and that "no further treatment" was necessary.
This confirms earlier prognoses suggesting the pope's cancer was caught early.
Pope Leo last week underwent surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung on October 13 at Rome's Gemelli hospital.
What did Pope Leo's doctors say about his health condition?
The 71-year-old pontiff's doctors said the final histopathology and molecular testing reports on the tissue removed during his surgery were issued on Wednesday.

"The results confirmed that the tumor was a lung adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localized. A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," the Holy See said.
What to know about Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer
The pope's surgeon added that there was "no clinical reason to cancel" the pope's visit to South America.
The ambitious trip, initially scheduled for November 6-17, would take the pontiff to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, involving a dozen flights, two helicopter rides and stops at high altitude.
Pope Leo's transparency around illness breaks with tradition
Leo was discharged from the hospital on Saturday, saying he would resume his activities gradually.
His illness shocked the Catholic Church, stoking concern that any potential prolonged treatment, such as radiotherapy or chemotherapy, could have affected the pope's ability to head the church.
Pope Leo first announced his condition during the traditional Sunday blessing on October 11, telling followers that he would be having a nodule surgically removed.
The announcement broke away from long-held traditions of secrecy surrounding papal health issues.
Pope Leo to undergo lung nodule surgery

articles.title: 'Rosal' slightly weakens; Batanes, Babuyan Islands under Signal No. 2
articles.summary: PAGASA said the center of Rosal's eye is estimated to be 495 kilometers east of Basco, Batanes.

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 7:15am
Satellite image from PAGASA showing Super Typhoon Rosal as of 4:40 a.m. on Oct. 22, 2026.
PAGASA / Released

MANILA, Philippines — Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) slightly weakened as it continued its northwestward track over the Philippine Sea east of Batanes, the state weather bureau PAGASA said.
As of 4 a.m. on Thursday, October 22, PAGASA said the center of Rosal's eye was estimated to be 495 kilometers east of Basco, Batanes.
Rosal now has maximum sustained winds of 195 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gusts of up to 240 kph, with a central pressure of 915 hPa.
It is moving northwestward at 20 kph, with Rosal’s strong to typhoon-force winds extending outward up to 780 kilometers from its center.

Despite its weakening, PAGASA maintained Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 in two areas, where estimated gale-force winds of 62 to 88 kph pose a minor to moderate threat to life and property within 24 hours:

items: Batanes
Northeastern portion of the Babuyan Islands

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over the following localities, where strong winds of 39 to 61 kph are expected within 36 hours:

items: Babuyan Islands: Remaining portion
Cagayan: Mainland
Isabela: Eastern portion (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, Dinapigue)
Ilocos Norte
Apayao

blocks.text: PAGASA noted that Signal No. 3 remains the highest warning level that may be raised over Batanes during Rosal's passage. However, should the typhoon shift to a more north-northwestward track, raising Signal No. 3 will become less likely.
Rosal entered the Philippine area of responsibility at 2 a.m., according to PAGASA.
Track forecast

Rosal is projected to continue moving northwestward until Friday morning, October 23. It will turn north-northwestward by Friday afternoon before recurving north-northeastward by Saturday, October 24.

The typhoon is expected to make its closest approach to Extreme Northern Luzon between Thursday afternoon and Friday morning. It is forecast to exit the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or early Saturday morning.
The state weather bureau expects Rosal to continue gradually weakening throughout the day, with a potential downgrade to typhoon status.
Rapid weakening is expected by Saturday, when the cyclone may be further downgraded to a severe tropical storm.

articles.title: German youth plan France-style mass protests
articles.summary: A youth-led movement in Germany has called for demonstrations in major cities of the country on October 31.

image.caption: A person carrying a placard that says "I want to live, not just survive" [FILE: December 2023]Image: Ying Tang/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Gen Z regelt" — or Gen Z's Got It — a youth initiative, has called for mass protests in 21 cities across Germany on Saturday, October 31; including Berlin, Cologne, Hamburg and Munich.
